comments.content: - **Build-blocking — `src/Mod/TechDraw/App/DrawViewPart.cpp:1503`**: All three new definitions (`isCosmeticVertex` at 1503, `isCosmeticEdge` at 1514, and `isCenterLine` at 1524) take only `std::string`, but their declarations in `DrawViewPart.h:244` are `static` functions taking both `App::DocumentObject*` and `std::string`. Compiling this translation unit fails with “no declaration matches” for each definition; callers using the declared signatures would also have no matching implementation to link against.

**1. DrawViewPart.h:242 vs DrawViewPart.cpp:1502 — `isCosmeticVertex` declaration and definition do not match (compile-breaking).**
Header declares `static bool isCosmeticVertex(App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element)`; the definition is `bool DrawViewPart::isCosmeticVertex(std::string element)` — one parameter vs two. Failure scenario: compiling DrawViewPart.cpp, the qualified-id matches no declaration in the class → hard error ("no declaration matches…"), the TechDraw App module cannot build, and every call site of the new API fails regardless of which shape it uses (a 2-arg call has no definition; a 1-arg call has no declaration).

**2. DrawViewPart.h:243 vs DrawViewPart.cpp:1513 — same mismatch for `isCosmeticEdge`.**
Declaration takes `(App::DocumentObject*, std::string)`, definition takes `(std::string)`. Same compile failure as item 1, independently blocking the build.

**3. DrawViewPart.h:244 vs DrawViewPart.cpp:1523 — same mismatch for `isCenterLine`.**
Declaration takes `(App::DocumentObject*, std::string)`, definition takes `(std::string)`. Same compile failure, third independent instance.

**4. DrawViewPart.h:242-244 vs DrawViewPart.cpp:1505, 1515, 1525 — declared `static` but bodies depend on `this`.**
The three declarations are `static`, yet the bodies call `getProjVertexByIndex(vertexIndex)` / `getEdge(element)` as unqualified member calls. A static member function has no `this`, so even if the parameter lists were reconciled, the bodies are ill-formed ("call to non-static member function without an object argument"). The patch embeds two incompatible designs — the old owner-carrying static API in the header and a new instance method in the .cpp — and contains no variant that compiles. Note the declared `owner` parameter is used by nothing in the patch; if anyone ever finished the header-side API, a caller passing a view different from the one whose state was inspected would silently get an answer about the wrong object.

**5. DrawUtil.h:252-254 / DrawUtil.cpp:1855-1888 — unconditional removal of three exported public static functions with zero call-site migration in the diff.**
`DrawUtil` is a `TechDrawExport` class and these were public API. Failure scenario: any translation unit outside these four files that still calls `DrawUtil::isCosmeticVertex(...)`, `isCosmeticEdge(...)`, or `isCenterLine(...)` (e.g. TechDrawGui selection/dimension code) fails to compile with "no member named…". I can point at the removal but not at the specific broken callers: the diff contains no call-site updates, and the rest of the repository is not present here, so I cannot confirm which TUs reference the removed symbols — if none exist, this item is moot.

Nothing else in the hunks is defective on its own merits: the moved bodies preserve the old logic (`getIndexFromName` → `getProjVertexByIndex`, source-type + `getCosmetic()` checks) exactly. One thing I could not check: whether the region of DrawViewPart.h the new declarations land in (between `progressValueChanged` and `public Q_SLOTS:`) is actually `public:` — the hunk context shows no access label, so I can't rule out the replacement API being non-public; that would be an additional defect if so.
